title: Northern Red Oak: Old Red Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Brussels Environment's own park guide gives up describing one of these and tells you to come in autumn. Six red oaks mapped, five of them in Europe.
intro: Brussels Environment's own walking route through the Parc d'Egmont gives up on describing its red oak and tells you to come back in autumn instead. That is the whole reason a North American tree ended up on European streets: nothing native turns that colour. Five of the six mapped here are European plantings and only one is at home, growing on the Spicebush Trail in a 50 acre patch of old forest inside the New York Botanical Garden. Milan has two, one beside the site of one of the city's six historic gates and one on a horse racing track that stopped racing a century ago and became a school. Prague's stands on the island where the city's archers used to practise. The Baarn oak, roughly 175 years old, wears a ring carrying words the municipality asked its residents to write in 2021.
